1.title: Jump in the Leaves
sounds: 입을 옆으로 살짝 벌리고 짧게 '에' 해요. '예스'처럼 길게 끌지 마요.
j는 입술을 살짝 내밀고 '쥬' 하듯 시작해요. '점프'의 'ㅈ'보다 입술이 둥글어요.
leaf는 끝이 f(바람 소리), leaves는 v에 z가 붙어 목이 울려요.
1.expression: Point at your hat, then jump a little higher on each 'jump'!

2.title: The Pumpkin Seeds
2.topic: carving a pumpkin and roasting the seeds with Dad (family, autumn)
sounds: -ed는 scooped처럼 t, carved처럼 d, tasted처럼 '이드' 세 가지로 나요.
baked는 '베이크-드' 두 박자가 아니라 '베익트' 한 박자로 끝내요.
s 다음의 c(k)는 바람을 거의 내지 않아 '스꿉트'에 가깝게 들려요.
2.expression: Make a funny face on “Yuck!”, then sound excited when Mia asks for another one.

3.title: Squirrels Get Ready for Winter
3.topic: how squirrels store nuts for winter and plant trees (animals, science)
lines: Have you ever *seen* a squirrel | running with a nut | in its *mouth*? ↗
In the fall, | squirrels are very *busy*.
They *collect* | *acorns*, | seeds, | and nuts | to eat in winter.
Then they *bury* them | in *hundreds* of different places.
They also *remember* | many of their *hiding spots*.
So a busy squirrel | is also | a *tree planter*! ↘
sounds: squirrel은 SKWUR-ul. r에서 혀를 뒤로 당기고, 끝 l은 혀끝을 윗니 뒤에 대요.
them again은 '데머겐', grow into는 '그로우인투'처럼 끊지 말고 이어 읽어요.
3.expression: Ask the first question like a curious science host, and sound amazed on the last line.

4.title: The Bus Stop Library
4.topic: a girl builds a little free library at her school bus stop (community, friendship)
lines: Every morning, | Rosa waited for the school bus | at the *corner* of Elm Street.
The other kids *stared* at their shoes | or *yawned*. | No one talked.
That weekend, | she and her *uncle* | built a *wooden box* | with a glass door.
They painted it *bright yellow* | and *nailed* it | to a post by the stop.
Rosa filled it | with *five* of her favorite *books*.
On the door, | she wrote: | “*Take* a book. | *Leave* a book.”
On Monday, | a shy boy named *Eli* | opened the door *slowly*.
By Friday, | the box was *empty*— | and then it was *full* again, | with books Rosa had never seen.
Someone even left a note: | “*Thank you*, | bus stop *librarian*!”
Now the kids at the corner | *trade* books | and talk about stories | until the bus *arrives*. ↘
sounds: “This bus stop is so boring,” (bored), “Can I really take one?” (shy), “Of course!” (cheerful)
해설은 차분하게, 로사는 처음엔 지루하게, 엘리는 수줍게, “Of course!”는 밝게 읽어요.
r은 혀가 아무 데도 닿지 않게, l은 혀끝을 윗니 뒤에 대요. really는 r과 l을 둘 다 연습해요.
4.expression: Let your voice change from bored to proud as the quiet bus stop comes alive.
events: Rosa waited every morning at a quiet, boring bus stop.
The kids at the stop never talked to each other.
Rosa and her uncle built a wooden box with a glass door.
They painted it yellow and nailed it to a post by the stop.
Rosa filled it with five books and wrote “Take a book. Leave a book.”
A shy boy named Eli asked if he could really take one.
By Friday the box was empty, then full of new books.
Now the kids trade books and talk about stories.
